data.notes_barbara:
Overlapping customer segment; Different products; Different business mix

Thryv serves small businesses with marketing and business-management tools. Customer overlap supports adjacency, but payroll/HCM is not its core offering.
data.notes_matthew: Thryv sells marketing and CRM (customer relationship management) software to small business owners and still gets about 40% of its revenue from Yellow Pages ads. No payroll or human resources product.

data.reason: Paylocity sells HR, payroll and finance/IT software on one HCM platform to employers (T:P1.2, T:P1.7). Thryv sells marketing software and done-for-you marketing services that help local service businesses get found online and win customers (C:P1.31, C:P1.2). The products serve different buyer needs: payroll and HR administration versus lead generation and marketing. Both sell subscriptions to US small and mid-sized businesses, but that overlap is generic. Thryv's buyers are mostly small local service firms (C:P1.19), and Paylocity's are mid-sized employers (T:P2.2).
Both serve local and small business owners, but Thryv sells marketing, lead conversion and online visibility tools and services rather than workforce administration software.
